commits.message:
DYD-658 implement: fail the Python campaign on any process's measurement failure

A sitecustomize startup or atexit finish failure now leaves a failure-*.txt
record beside the campaign config, naming the process's pid, phase and
command line; collect raises on any record instead of combining the rest.
A process that cannot write its record exits 70 rather than running on as
if measured. Processes without DYDO_PYTHON_COVERAGE_CONFIG stay silent.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

DYD-658 fix: record measurement failures over collect's loopback port

A process whose measurement fails at startup or finish now sends its record
to a loopback port that collect listens on while the command runs
(DYDO_PYTHON_COVERAGE_FAILURES), instead of writing failure-*.txt beside the
config. The record no longer depends on the output being writable or on
any parent passing a nonzero exit on. A reader thread takes the records in
connection order until collect's own end mark. If it stops early, the
campaign fails. A process that cannot send its record still exits 70.

Regressions: end-to-end collect with an exit-ignoring driver whose failing
child cannot write beside its config, at startup and at finish (red on
e7d28efe); a record the reader cannot decode fails the campaign.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

DYD-658 fix: hold one reporting connection per measured process from startup

Each measured campaign process now opens its reporting connection to
collect at startup, names itself on it, and holds it until exit. The port
comes from DYDO_PYTHON_COVERAGE_FAILURES or, if that variable is gone,
from the port mirrored in config.json. A failure at startup or finish goes
on the already-open connection, so descriptor exhaustion at finish no
longer loses it. collect reads newline-framed records with a selector and
never blocks on a peer. After the command returns it waits at most
_SETTLE_SECONDS (5 s) for connections to close, then fails on any failure
record, any unreadable or incomplete record, and any connection still
open. A connection that closes with no failure (a clean exit or a killed
process) passes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

DYD-658 fix: open the reporting connection inside the startup failure boundary

Socket creation, port lookup and connect now run inside _Report's
constructor, so an error there never reaches site's continue-unmeasured
handler. A refused, reset or timed-out connect, or one short of an
ephemeral port, is retried: four attempts of at most 0.1 s each, with
10/20/40 ms backoff, 0.47 s worst case. A process that still has no
connection, or cannot create its socket (EMFILE), exits 70 at startup
before its program runs. No measured program runs without its
connection. The exit-70 path allocates no new descriptor.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

DYD-658 fix: exit 70 when the generated sitecustomize cannot import python_coverage

The sitecustomize that collect generates first checks
DYDO_PYTHON_COVERAGE_CONFIG through os.environ. Without it, it imports
nothing, so a process with no campaign config stays silent. With it, a
python_coverage import that raises (or is missing) ends the process with
os._exit(70) before its program runs. Before, site printed "Error in
sitecustomize" and ran the program unmeasured. os and sys are already
loaded, so the exit needs no new resource. The stderr line is best effort.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

DYD-658 merge: feature/dydo-3-6-0 at 88f12b05

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

DYD-658 fix: tests take a failed process's pid from the process itself, not from Popen

Hosted python-coverage (windows-latest) failed 11 test_python_coverage cases (run 42120732020):
each stderr carried the right record, naming the pid the measured process runs as, while the test
expected Popen.pid. A Windows venv's Scripts\python.exe is a redirector that runs the base
interpreter as a child process of its own, so the two differ there.

The one measured child whose failure a test names now gets a sitecustomize of its own that writes
os.getpid() to failed.pid before running the startup under test (the campaign's generated text, or
the case's own); the outliving child prints its pid on its ready line. Every assertion about the
campaign failing, naming the process, exiting 70 and not running the program is unchanged.
Production records already name the in-process pid and are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

DYD-658 fix: wrapped test children run the startup file collect generates, not a copy of it

The pid-witness sitecustomize records os.getpid(), then reads and runs <output>/startup/sitecustomize.py
as collect wrote it; the connection-fault setups run that file too. A generated startup that loses its
import-failure guard, or starts no measurement, now turns the wrapped cases red.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

DYD-658 fix: collect puts its own site-packages on the campaign path, so base-interpreter children are measured

A child started with sys._base_executable inherits the campaign env but not the venv's packages, so it could
not import coverage.py and failed the campaign (hosted Windows: test_control_dydo_lifetime, test_windows_job's
nested owner). collect now adds the collecting interpreter's purelib and platlib, deduplicated, after startup
and tools and before the inherited PYTHONPATH. A process that still cannot import coverage still fails.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

DYD-658 fix: a measured process searches the collector's packages last and only to import coverage.py, so no caller package is shadowed

354caf8c put the collecting interpreter's purelib and platlib on the campaign PYTHONPATH, ahead of the
inherited path and of every child's own site-packages. A caller's package of a name the collector also
has (six) was replaced by the collector's, and a command failing on the caller's version passed.

collect now leaves PYTHONPATH as before 354caf8c (startup, tools, inherited) and names those paths as
`packages` in config.json. _start reads the config first, appends `packages` to the end of sys.path for
`import coverage` only and removes them again. A child of the base interpreter is still measured with
the collector's coverage.py, but its program searches exactly the path it would unmeasured: a module
it lacks stays missing. A process that still cannot measure, such as CPython 3.13, fails by name.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

DYD-658 fix: report interrupted finish on the held connection

Catch BaseException during finish, report it through the existing connection,
and re-raise. Cover KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit and the RuntimeError control
at receipt writing, and qualify import search-path transparency.

DYD-658 fix: drain the exit observer before child termination

Read the side observer concurrently and acknowledge its half-close before
os._exit, preserving the still-connected campaign failure assertions on
Windows as well as Linux.
